diagram.title: Checkpointed TPU job launcher lifecycle from warmup to zero-drift resume
diagram.prediction: Why must the warmup compilation step run before the timed step loop without overwriting the restored checkpoint state?
diagram.reading: Read top to bottom: the launcher loads either the initial state or `checkpoint-latest.json`, runs one synchronized `@jax.jit` warmup call to compile XLA HLO without mutating state, executes timed steady-state steps while appending to `events.jsonl`, and writes `checkpoint-latest.json` atomically via `.tmp` + `fsync` + `os.replace`.
diagram.alt: Read top to bottom: initialize or restore checkpoint state, run synchronized warmup compilation without mutating state, execute timed steps logging events.jsonl, and atomically replace checkpoint-latest.json.
diagram.scope: Conceptual / analytic teaching diagram; not a recorded benchmark.

nodes.label: Init or --resume: load (step, w, b, m_w, m_b, key) + state_hash
Warmup: compile @jax.jit train_step + block_until_ready (no state mutation)
Steady loop: timed step + block_until_ready -> append events.jsonl
